method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government) 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP' (produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025)), 22 claims; LICENCE: ©ASHM 2025 (the PDF states copyright only, with no reuse terms; the ASHM Copyright & Disclaimer page returned 404 on 2026-09-23) (read at the copyright line on the back matter of the PDF (ISBN 978-1-921850-97-4) and the hiv.guidelines.org.au footer). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)' (version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24)), 12 claims; LICENCE: © EACS, 2026 - All Rights Reserved (page footer); EACS permits downloading the guidelines for own use and reproducing a portion for educational purposes with referencing (read at the page footer of the eacs.sanfordguide.com PrEP page and the EACS guidelines page (https://www.eacsociety.org/guidelines/eacs-guidelines/)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the European AIDS Clinical Society guidelines v13.0 (2025) PrEP section from the web edition (EACS v13.0 has no PDF); every S1 claim is unchanged. S2 is all-rights-reserved, so it is paraphrased and hash-anchored. S2 was chosen over the WHO 2025 lenacapavir guideline (NCBI Bookshelf copy behind a reCAPTCHA challenge) because it also covers oral PrEP, monitoring and hepatitis B.

claims.claim: **Any GP, other medical specialist or authorised nurse practitioner can prescribe PrEP under a PBS streamlined authority;** no specialist training is needed.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not talk people out of PrEP;** a prescriber who is uncomfortable should refer straight away to a colleague or service that provides it. Raise PrEP proactively when a sexual history shows HIV risk, even if the visit is about something else.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer PrEP to people with HIV risk in the past 3 months who expect similar risk over the next 3 months,** and also to people with no recent risk whose circumstances have changed so that they now foresee risk in the next 3 months.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Document a negative HIV test first, using a fourth-generation antigen/antibody venous blood test done within 7 days of the PrEP assessment;** the person should start PrEP within 7 days of that negative test. A rapid point-of-care test is not enough on its own.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not start PrEP in someone with symptoms or signs of acute HIV, or with an indeterminate HIV result, until HIV is excluded:** starting in undiagnosed acute infection has led to resistance, most often to emtricitabine.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A recent high-risk exposure beyond the 72-hour nPEP window:** start PrEP and watch for seroconversion with fourth-generation tests over the next 2–8 weeks, then return to routine monitoring.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Kidneys: check creatinine, eGFR, urine protein:creatinine ratio and blood pressure at baseline, and assess CKD risk factors.** Starting PrEP when the eGFR is well established below 60 mL/min/1.73m² is not recommended, as there are no data.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A new eGFR around 60 at baseline: repeat it within 7 days,** fasting or without a cooked-meat meal in the previous 4 hours. If it stays just above or below 60, talk to a PrEP specialist: PrEP may still be possible with close monitoring, and on-demand dosing may suit.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hepatitis A, B and C serology at the start; vaccinate against hepatitis A and B where susceptible.** Refer newly found chronic hepatitis B or C for treatment assessment; neither diagnosis is a barrier to starting PrEP.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use only co-formulated tenofovir disoproxil with emtricitabine,** the only combination licensed for PrEP in Australia. Never substitute or add any other antiretroviral, and never prescribe PrEP for someone not under your care (no expedited partner therapy).
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Daily PrEP can be offered to anyone at risk.** It is the only schedule recommended for cisgender women, transgender women on oestrogen, transgender men who have vaginal sex, and people who inject drugs.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **On-demand dosing: two tablets 2–24 hours before sex, then single tablets at 24 hours and at 48 hours, both timed from the first dose.** If sex goes on over several days, keep taking one tablet every 24 hours, and take one on each of the two days after the last sex. Not TGA-approved.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer on-demand PrEP to cisgender men (whatever the sex of their partners) and to trans and gender-diverse people who were male-assigned at birth and take no oestradiol-based hormones,** when they prefer it, their risky sex happens under twice weekly or unpredictably, and they can put sex off by 2 hours.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Not on-demand for cisgender women** (tissue levels are inadequate), not for protection from injecting, and with caution in adolescent MSM, where it has not been trialled and daily adherence has been poor.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The 'Ts and Ss' schedule (single doses on Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday) is not recommended,** because no trial has tested it.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Review every 3 months: repeat the HIV test at each refill and prescribe no more than 90 days at a time.** The first script may be filled on the day the baseline HIV blood is taken, provided the laboratory reliably returns a fourth-generation result in 24–48 hours. On-demand users should still attend quarterly for HIV and STI testing.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recheck eGFR 3 months after starting, then every 6 months;** monitor more closely in people over 40, with baseline eGFR under 90, with hypertension or diabetes, or on nephrotoxic drugs.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask about adherence at every visit.** If someone repeatedly takes fewer than four tablets a week on daily PrEP, enough to undermine its protection and their safety, stop prescribing it.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before starting (EACS):** a documented negative fourth-generation test from the preceding week or the same day, plus a plasma HIV RNA test at or before the start (or restart) when there was high-risk exposure in the previous 6 weeks or long-acting PrEP is planned. In someone at high risk, waiting for the RNA result should not hold up the start.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Testing and scripts on PrEP (EACS):** repeat a fourth-generation test one month in, then at intervals of 2–4 months. Stable users on daily PrEP for more than a year can have prescriptions of up to 6 months, with an interim test done without a clinic visit.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **At the first clinical signs of seroconversion or a positive HIV test, switch at once to standard three-drug ART with no gap,** and refer to a specialist HIV unit if needed.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Offer hepatitis A, hepatitis B, HPV and mpox vaccines to everyone on PrEP, and doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis where indicated;** screen for syphilis, chlamydia, gonorrhoea, hepatitis A and hepatitis C at the start and regularly.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Kidneys (EACS):** test kidney function at some point in the first 3 months. The people most in need of systematic renal monitoring on TDF are those over 50 and those with existing renal impairment; on-demand dosing may be kinder to the kidneys than daily.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Daily start: two tablets together, then one a day;** by pharmacokinetic data, two tablets reach protective levels in all compartments within 2 hours. EACS lists TAF/FTC 25/200 mg daily as an option when kidney function or bone density rule out TDF/FTC.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Stopping (EACS):** men finish with one tablet at 24 hours and one at 48 hours after their last sex; for everyone else, pharmacokinetic studies support a further 7 days of daily TDF/FTC after the last exposure.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **On-demand dosing (EACS):** trial evidence is only in MSM and transgender women, but EACS regards pharmacokinetic studies as supporting it for women and people who inject drugs too.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Poor adherence plus condomless at-risk sex calls for PEP.** Poor adherence means under 4 pills a week on daily PrEP, or not following 2-1-1 on demand. While PEP is being arranged, take two PrEP tablets as soon as possible and then one a day until seen.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Long-acting options abroad (EACS):** cabotegravir 600 mg intramuscular monthly for two doses then every two months (optional 1-month oral lead-in of 30 mg daily; one week of overlapping oral PrEP or condoms after the first injection); lenacapavir 927 mg subcutaneous every 6 months with a two-day oral load of 600 mg a day, and 300 mg weekly by mouth if an injection is over 14 days late.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Long-acting cabotegravir can blunt viral load and antibody responses, so breakthrough HIV may be missed or found late;** repeat both HIV RNA and fourth-generation tests. Neither cabotegravir nor lenacapavir treats hepatitis B, so vaccinate against it before long-acting PrEP.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hepatitis B (EACS):** EACS recommends daily, not on-demand, PrEP for people with chronic hepatitis B, given limited evidence on reactivation and resistance. Missing HBV serology should not delay oral PrEP. If PrEP stops, test HBV DNA and liver enzymes no less often than 3-monthly, for 12 months or more.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)', version 13.0, 2025 (web page read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-pre-exposure-prophylaxis, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Chronic hepatitis B no longer rules out on-demand PrEP;** daily PrEP should be offered and on-demand may be considered in some circumstances. Counsel strict adherence to avoid a hepatitis flare and HBV resistance.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Stopping tenofovir/emtricitabine in chronic hepatitis B can cause a severe flare.** An experienced hepatitis B clinician should assess the person before PrEP stops, followed by close monitoring.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Stopping safely:** cisgender men can stop daily PrEP by taking a dose 24 and 48 hours after the last at-risk sex; on-demand users take one tablet a day for 2 days after the last sex. Everyone else on daily PrEP should continue for 28 days after the last exposure.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before restarting after a break, repeat the HIV test** in case HIV was acquired while off PrEP.
claims.locator: ASHM Health (funded by the Australian Government), 'ASHM National PrEP Guidelines 2025: Prevent HIV by Prescribing PrEP', produced July 2025 (web edition last updated August 2025), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/ASHM-PrEP-guidelines-2025_FINAL.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23
